The working principle is “Ask before filling a gap with a guess.”

Give the reviewer a complete handoff

  • Read the original note.

  • Check the assigned owner.

  • Keep the source link.

  • Name the next action.

  • State the remaining caveat.

  • Ask about missing context.

  • Preserve the earlier record.

Preserve the reasoning behind each handoff

When a request arrives, read the original note before choosing a label. Check whether the author has named an owner and preserve that name in the handoff. Use the checklist to identify missing context, then ask a focused question rather than guessing. Keep the source note linked beside the summary so another colleague can inspect it. If the request changes, update the next action and explain the change without deleting the record or making a promise on behalf of someone else.
